title: Approve this phone
summary: Approves a new phone with a device that is already signed in, so the new phone gets the message history (rule 5). The new phone asks; the old device shows who asks and approves after a biometric check; both compare the same symbols (Matrix SAS verification).

deviceId.description: The Matrix device ID of the other device.

displayName.description: Its device name, for example the phone model.

role.description: newPhone: this phone wants the history. approver: this device holds the history and got a request.

phase.description: requesting and waitingForOther: newPhone sent the request. incoming: approver got it. confirmIdentity: approver passes the biometric check. compare: both show symbols. waitingForMatch: this side confirmed, the other not yet.

request.effect: newPhone: SessionVerificationController.requestDeviceVerification. Sets phase waitingForOther. Then POST /v1/me/approval-nudge (bipe-chat/bipe#628), so the other devices of the account get a push. A nudge failure does not change the phase.

notifyAgain.effect: newPhone, phase waitingForOther, from accounts.approvalNudgeAgainSeconds (registries) after the last nudge: POST /v1/me/approval-nudge again. Shows bipe_app_verify_notify_again. A rate_limited answer is ignored.

receive.effect: approver: SessionVerificationControllerDelegate.didReceiveVerificationRequest with SessionVerificationRequestDetails. Acknowledges it and shows phase incoming over the app.

accept.effect: approver: asks for a biometric check (or the device PIN), then acceptVerificationRequest. The new phone starts SAS (startSasVerification) when the accept arrives.

decline.effect: approver: declineVerification. The new phone shows cancelled.

match.effect: Both: the symbols are the same. approveVerification. phase done after didFinish.

noMatch.effect: Both: the symbols differ. declineVerification; nothing is approved; shows bipe_app_verify_mismatch.

cancel.effect: cancelVerification at any time before done.

notes: Only for devices of the same account (requestDeviceVerification). Verifying other people is not part of phase 1.

The approver sees the other device's name and time before anything else, and a biometric check comes before the accept (ADR 0059 QR approval rule, applied here too). bipe_device_approval_never_for_others shows on the incoming screen.
Symbols and their labels come from the SDK (Matrix spec SAS, m.sas.v1). The labels are in English; show the symbol large and the label small.
The new phone that comes back through QR from the old phone (bipe-chat/bipe#203, #573) needs no verification: the QR login already shares the secrets.
When Encryption.hasDevicesToVerifyAgainst is false, the new phone does not offer this screen; encryption-status offers only the recovery key.

Approval nudge (bipe-chat/bipe#628): Matrix sends the request as a to-device event, and the homeserver does not push to-device events. So after request the new phone calls POST /v1/me/approval-nudge. bipe-api pushes to the other devices of the account that have a Bipe Next pusher (notification-service, kind deviceApproval). The push only opens Bipe there: the sync then delivers the request and receive shows phase incoming. The push approves nothing and carries no device name.
notifyAgain shows on the waiting screen only when the account has another device. A device with notifications off gets no push; the text bipe_app_verify_body stays the instruction for that case.
